maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, the question asked by the hon. member for Levis is precisely the same question as was asked in committee on another bill only two days ago of the Minister of Finance, who perhaps is not overly courteous in his answers but who did not hesitate for one second and did not object in the least to this question. We know that certain hon. members supporting the government have declared in the house that this legislation is of doubtful constitutionality. No less a member than the hon. member for Bellechasse has questioned the whole constitutional basis of this legislation, and we know the respect in which the hon. member for Bellechasse as a lawyer is held by hon. gentlemen opposite. In view of the question the hon. member for Bellechasse has raised with respect to the constitutionality of the bill it seems to me it is perfectly proper that my hon. friend should ask the minister if he has consulted the law officers of the crown and
Trans-Canada Highway Act satisfied himself that the legislation he is asking parliament to enact is within the power of parliament to enact.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, it is out of order for my hon. friend to ask that question at this time, but for his information may I say that this bill, like any bill introduced by this administration, is constitutional.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Thank you very much.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Clause agreed to.
On clause 2-Aggregate limited to $400 million.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: This clause provides that the aggregate of all expenditures under certain sections of the act shall not exceed $400 million. I should like to ask the minister whether in reaching this estimate of $400 million provision has been made to cover the share of the province of Quebec should it decide to sign an agreement or is this amount of $400 million limited to the nine provinces that now have agreements?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I did not get the end of the hon. member's question. I should have been paying more attention. Did he ask whether the $50 million of the total of $400 million to be expended, $350 million having already been voted, is to be expended on all nine provinces?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Ten.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: The answer to that is that the $400 million will be expended on those provinces which are signatories to the Trans-Canada Highway Act.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: In order to arrive at the amount of $400 million an estimate must have been made by the minister's department. In reaching the estimate of $400 million was consideration given only to the nine provinces now under this scheme or was provision made for the province of Quebec should it decide to enter into an agreement?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, all we can deal with are the facts. At the present time we have nine signatories to the Trans-Canada Highway Act, and the approximation of $400 million as the total amount to be paid out to these nine provinces is the approximation we have at the present time. We have nothing else to deal with. We have no other signatory except the nine provinces. So far only nine provinces have made any expenditures.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
I should like to put the
question in a somewhat different way. Is it anticipated that the whole or practically the

Trans-Canada Highway Act whole of this $400 million will be required for the nine provinces that now have agreements?

speakerposition: Minister of Labour
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: That is what he said.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: No, that is not what he said.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I think I have answered that question.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I should like the minister to answer that question yes or no. After all, whatever Your Honour may say about clause 1, clause 2 is asking parliament to vote money and surely there should be no equivocation about what we are voting the money for. We are now dealing with $400 million which is a lot of the taxpayers' money.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Fifty million dollars.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: It is true, as the minister interjects, that only $50 million is now being voted but even $50 million in my book is a lot of money. We are entitled to know whether the estimate of $400 million is in respect of the nine agreements in existence and no money is being provided in case Quebec should sign.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: He has answered that.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Let the minister himself answer it.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: He has.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I do not think he has.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: You should listen.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Perhaps the hon. member might listen since he has no other contribution to make to the committee.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I must ask hon. members not to interrupt the hon. member who has the floor.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
I say that if we are to be
treated with anything but contempt we are entitled to know whether this $400 million is the estimate for a complete road in the nine provinces or whether it is an estimate for a complete trans-Canada highway across the whole of Canada.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I hate to be offending my hon. friend when he seems to be getting angry and charges me with contempt. I do not know whether it is contempt of him or contempt of the house. There is a great difference. I want to assure my hon. friend that I do not have contempt but the greatest respect and admiration for him and also, it goes without saying, for the other members of the house. But much as I should like to please my hon. friend, who has great
[Mr. Pickersgill.!

experience in the art of cross-examination and who demands a yes or no answer just like that, with my limited powers of expression I cannot amplify in any more concise manner than I have already done, even at the risk of further hurting the feelings of my hon. and distinguished friend.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: May I ask the minister how the amount of $50 million is arrived at by provinces? An estimate must have been made in each of the participating provinces and I should like to know how this amount is arrived at by provinces.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: In reply to the hon. member for Levis, may I say that the engineers have taken the amounts that each of the nine provinces has spent to date, added to them the estimates of the amounts which the provinces anticipate they will spend in the next three years and have come to an approximate figure of $400 million as the amount which the dominion government is providing to contribute to the trans-Canada highway to ensure its completion.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Has the minister any assurance that the $50 million we are now voting will be sufficient to cover the completion of the trans-Canada highway in these nine provinces?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
Seeing that we are not building the highway but that each of the nine provinces is building its respective share and having regard to the unfortunate experience of the former minister of public works, Mr. Winters, whose able parliamentary assistant was the hon. member for Levis, and his false calculations as to when the highway would be completed and as to the cost of the highway, I should not like to put myself on record as being definite on the result. Mr. Winters was so far off the mark that I would not want, three years from now, to be in the same position.
As to the figures we have and as to the knowledge we have at the present time, we anticipate that this sum of $400 million will approximately complete the contribution of the federal government to the trans-Canada highway, with the possible exception of the adopted province of my friend the hon. member for Bonavista-Twillingate, namely Newfoundland.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
I do not think the minister has answered the question put to him by the hon. member for Levis. The hon. member has asked what amount was being estimated to be spent out of this $400 million or out of this $50 million additional we are being asked to pass today, or what amount is being allocated to each of the provinces under the scheme. We definitely know that all of that

money is not going to go to one or two provinces. We should like to know approximately what the estimate is for each of the provinces.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: It has not been allocated yet. It is impossible to allocate these things until the time comes. It is a pool from which money will be spent if it is needed and as proof is given by each of the provinces that the expense has been incurred.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: The minister was making a comparison with Mr. Winters. We have here an item of $50 million. We do not know, according to the minister's answer, where it comes from or how it is made up. I hope the minister will recall the day when he was in another committee. I should like to ask this question and I think it is a fair one. Surely the calculation must have been made in order to arrive at the amount of $50 million. That is not $5; it is $50 million. Surely the engineers in the department must have the figures from each province and the minister should be able to tell us how much is going to be spent by provinces in the next three years.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I want to thank my hon. friend and tell him that if I came as close as he did I would be $150 million out. His minister, seconded by himself, was of the opinion that the trans-Canada highway would cost $250 million. It is going to cost $400 million.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Your previous minister did not say anything last year.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Let my hon. friend keep his temper and I will read him the answer he wants. This is all going to be very nice and very friendly. It is now estimated that Canada will be called upon to contribute the following amounts to the provinces: Newfoundland, $30 million; Prince Edward Island, $7.5 million; Nova Scotia, $25.5 million; New Brunswick, $46 million; Ontario, $120 million; Manitoba, $21 million; Saskatchewan, $15.5 million; Alberta, $23.5 million; British Columbia, $111 million. In the schedules which were filed the other day when this matter last came before the committee, the amounts which have been committed for each of the provinces have been set out. I trust that answers my hon. friend's question.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
I should just like to draw the committee's attention to the fact, since the strictly non-partisan references were made by the minister, that we have had amending legislation brought into the House of Commons by the minister's predecessor only a short time ago and that these mistakes in time and mistakes in date at which the road would be completed and so on were all
Trans-Canada Highway Act made by the minister's illustrious predecessor. It seems to me that the reference was quite uncalled for. But since it has been made it seems to me that the whole record should be put straight.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Shall clause 2 carry?

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: No. Before this clause carries may I ask the minister whether this $120 million allotted to Ontario is sufficient to complete the northern route of the trans-Canada highway or that which we now use as the trans-Canada highway and at the same time will it be enough to complete the southern route which is not completed as yet?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: In reply to the hon. member for Timiskaming may I say that this sum of money would involve the participation by Ontario from border to border in the present trans-Canada highway.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: My question is in relationship to the fact that we have in Ontario a northern trans-Canada route and also what is considered to be just a trans-Canada route. The northern route is now the route that is in use and it is not completed or at least not up to standard. At the same time it is expected that there will be a permanent southern route from Agawa up through Sault Ste. Marie. What I am asking is whether there is in this $120 million enough money for the federal contribution to complete the section we now use and to complete the new section.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: This sum pertains to the only designated trans-Canada highway which is in the process of being built at the present time and which is set out in particular in schedule A in the contract between the dominion and the Ontario government. I appreciate the fact that my friend the hon. member for Timiskaming would like to have built a second trans-Canada northern route; but as he can appreciate, at the present time we cannot contemplate anything else except the completion of the first trans-Canada highway, and that is what this is for.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: The minister may be aware of the fact that we are already using the northern route. It is a complete highway across Canada. But we should like the assurance that it is going to be brought up to regular standards along with the proposed route.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
The province which fairly well had the fixing of this route did not designate the route to which my hon. friend is referring as part of the trans-Canada highway.

Trans-Canada Highway Act

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: A sign was put up by the department saying it was the northern route of the trans-Canada highway.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I have been most restrained, Mr. Chairman, but seeing that hon. members from other provinces are making certain that the interests of their provinces are protected in this legislation-

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I think we need some of that particular brew which my hon. friend is going to use for the completion of this trans-Canada highway. We might use it to complete this debate.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
I apologize for my fit of
coughing, for the relief of which I have been handed a glass of water. Can the minister inform the house whether sufficient provision is made in this bill to meet the needs for the completion of the trans-Canada highway in British Columbia?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: We would certainly hope so. But you have a very volatile minister of highways out there called Mr. Gaglardi. If he spent more time in completing this highway than he spends in talking we would get along with it a great deal faster. We have allocated for British Columbia $111 million as an estimate of the contribution of the dominion which is more than one quarter of all the money being spent on this trans-Canada highway. It is sadly behind in its allocation.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I would like to pursue the question asked by the hon. member for Kootenay West when speaking about British Columbia. Is there enough money to meet the needs of the province of Quebec if and when the government of that province decides to come into the plan?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: I have no more questions to ask; I just want to express one regret, and that is that the province of Quebec has been forgotten.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Shall clause 2 carry?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext: Just before clause 2 carries, I also would like to express regret that the minister and the Prime Minister have completely repudiated the undertakings given to the people of Newfoundland by the provincial leader of their party in the name of the Prime Minister in the provincial election last year, and to say that considering the sacrifices that gentleman made, the unavailing sacrifices for their party, it is pretty shabby treatment.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Minister responsible for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; Minister responsible for National Capital Commission
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, just in reply to that, the Prime Minister of Canada and myself as Minister of Public Works are doing

everything in our power to fulfil just as rapidly as the premier of Newfoundland makes it possible for us to do so our obligations in regard to the trans-Canada highway. I do not think it is amiss to say that the contribution of the dominion to that trans-Canada highway in Newfoundland constitutes a tremendously larger sum than the contribution of the province of Newfoundland. I have nothing but sympathy for the desire of the Newfoundlanders that this part of the highway should be completed; but if their premier in his wisdom chooses to squander the money given his province by the dominion, properly designated to his province by the dominion, on so many odds and ends-

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY ACT AMENDMENTS TO EXTEND PERIOD OF PAYMENTS AND INCREASE MAXIMUM EXPENDITURES

speakeroldname: Hon. Alvin Hamilton (Minister of Northern Affairs and National Resources):
speakerposition: Minister of Northern Affairs and National Resources
subtopic: INCREASE IN COUNCIL MEMBERSHIP- CHANGES RESPECTING COURTS, ETC.
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, the resolution is largely self-explanatory, and I need not take up the time of the house with extended comments at this stage.
This legislation deals with three broad subjects. The first is the constitution of the territorial council. It is proposed to increase the membership of the council to reflect the increasing population of the territory, to remove an existing requirement that the commissioner must sit apart from the council, and to provide for the establishment of an advisory committee on finance. This committee, composed of council members, will advise on the

Yukon Act
preparation of the territorial budget, and may be consulted on other matters of policy arising between council sessions.
As I told the house a year ago, consideration has been given to ways in which it might be possible to work toward fully separate judicial systems suited to territorial requirements. The object is ultimately to reach the pattern already established in the provinces. This bill constitutes a court of appeal for the Yukon which can ultimately and easily develop toward the provincial pattern as circumstances permit.
Certain changes in the constitution of the territorial court are also proposed. These will make the judge of the Northwest Territories court ex officio also a judge of the court of the Yukon Territory, authorize the appointment and remuneration of deputy judges as required, and provide for other minor or consequential changes in judicial arrangements.
I may say that parallel changes in judicial arrangements for the Northwest Territories will be proposed in separate legislation. Taken together, the new provisions for territorial courts and courts of appeal should enable a better service to be provided to litigants and others in both territories.
The other matter with which the bill deals is the application of territorial ordinances to all residents of the Yukon Territory. Some question has been raised about this, particularly with regard to game, and the bill is designed to clarify the power of the territorial council in this respect.
I think, Mr. Chairman, that when hon. members have had an opportunity to examine the bill they will find the proposed changes fully consistent with the orderly development of the territory as a separate Canadian entity, in accordance with the wishes of the territorial council, and with the best interests of the residents.

speechtext: I should like to ask the minister if plans are under way for developing provincial autonomy in the two territories and, if so, how long a period is expected to elapse before these territories will be able to form provinces of their own?

speakerposition: Minister of Northern Affairs and National Resources
subtopic: INCREASE IN COUNCIL MEMBERSHIP- CHANGES RESPECTING COURTS, ETC.
speechtext:
It is, I think the hope of all Canadians that as soon as economic conditions warrant, new provinces will be formed in the present territory of Yukon and the Northwest Territories.
I think it is also reasonable to assume that before they become provinces they will have to have sufficient economic resources of their own to run their own administration. That is not presently possible. There have been many speculations as to when this eventuality may come about; I think that is all it can be at this time: speculation. We are hopeful that new mining developments, new oil and gas developments will make it possible to have new communities in certain parts of the north. When these communities are sufficiently established and give evidence that they can support a provincial government we would, I think, be happy to consider such a proposal from them.
Another aspect of the question is that the people in the Yukon and the Northwest Territories have already developed a considerable spirit of autonomy. They want the right to run their own affairs; they resent very strongly the suggestion that provinces should take them over. I think it follows from all this that they themselves should make the decision.
I do not know whether that answers in full what the hon. member had in mind, but I think it represents the thinking on this matter at the present time.

speakerposition: Minister of Northern Affairs and National Resources
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING COURTS, JUDGES AND GAME LEGISLATION
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I think the hon. member has probably confused two things. There is an act called the Territorial Lands Act which clearly defines and limits the boundaries for administering land. This does stop at the mainland coast of North America and follows around the shores of Hudson bay and into Ungava bay. It takes in all the islands up to the low water mark. As far as government, justice, and game are concerned, the Northwest Territories Act defines the boundaries of that area for political and administrative purposes. I happen to have the act here and will read the relevant section:
2.	(k) "Territories" means the Northwest Territories, which comprise
(i)	all that part of Canada north of the 60th parallel of north latitude, except the portions thereof within the Yukon Territory and the provinces of Quebec and Newfoundland, and
(ii)	the islands in Hudson Bay, James bay and Ungava bay, except those islands within the provinces of Manitoba, Ontario and Quebec.
For political administration purposes the Northwest Territories under this act is all the area north of the sixtieth parallel except the Yukon and except any areas of Quebec or Newfoundland which are above the sixtieth parallel but does include all the islands in Ungava and in James and Hudson bays. Therefore, they are two separate matters.

speechtext:
First Communique
The first plenary sessions of the meeting of commonwealth prime ministers were held at 10, Downing street, today.
In opening the meeting, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom expressed, on behalf of his commonwealth colleagues, their deep sorrow at the circumstances which had prevented Dr. Verwoerd, the Prime Minister of South Africa, from carrying out his intention of attending this meeting. He also expressed his regret that the Prime Minister of Ceylon was prevented, owing to the impending election, from coming to London at this time.
Mr. Macmillan welcomed the Prime Minister of Malaya, Tuanku Abdul Rahman, as the first representative of Malaya to attend a commonwealth prime ministers' meeting since Malaya attained full membership of the commonwealth.
The reply to Mr. Macmillan's opening statement was made by Tuanku Abdul Rahman. In the course of his reply he raised the problem of racial discrimination in South Africa, and its effects on relations between South Africa and other commonwealth countries, and he expressed the hope that opportunity would be found for the commonwealth prime ministers to discuss this while they were in London.
The representative of the South African government, Mr. Eric Louw, emphasized that sole responsibility for domestic policies within South Africa rested with the union government.
The meeting reaffirmed the traditional practice that commonwealth conferences do not discuss the internal affairs of member countries. Mr. Louw expressed his readiness to meet other heads of delegations informally for discussion of this problem. Arrangements are being made accordingly.
After these procedural questions had been settled Mr. Macmillan opened a general discussion on the world political situation. The Prime Minister of India and the President of Pakistan continued this discussion at the afternoon session. It will be resumed at a further plenary session tomorrow morning.
3rd May, 1960.
Final Communique
The meeting of commonwealth prime ministers ended today. Pakistan was represented
by its President. The United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, Ghana, the Federation of Malaya and the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland were represented by their Prime Ministers. South Africa was represented by the Minister of External Affairs, and Ceylon by the Minister of Justice.
2.	This was the tenth of these meetings to have been held since the war. It has taken place at a time of great significance to the commonwealth and to the world.
3.	The continuing growth of the membership of the commonwealth was marked by the attendance at this meeting of the Prime Minister of the Federation of Malaya, which achieved independence in August, 1957. The representatives of the other commonwealth countries welcomed the presence of the federation at the conference.
4.	The commonwealth is an association of independent sovereign states, each responsible for its own policies; but the primary objective of all is world peace and security. It is their declared purpose to do everything in their power to achieve that objective, and to continue to co-operate to that end with all the peace-loving nations of the world.
5.	In this spirit the commonwealth ministers have reviewed the major international problems of the day, on the eve of the impending summit conference which is to be attended by the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. They expressed their sincere hopes for a successful outcome of that conference as a further step in the relaxation of international tension. They discussed, in particular, the problem of disarmament; and they welcomed the progress made at the Geneva conference on the discontinuance of nuclear weapons tests. They hoped that, on the basis of the preliminary work already done, the summit conference would be able to make some significant progress toward an eventual settlement, under international control, of the problem of disarmament. An advance toward a solution of that problem, linked with a progressive lessening of political tensions, would afford a firm basis for strengthening confidence between nations and promoting world security.
6.	The commonwealth ministers also discussed the problems of Africa, the Middle East, the Far East and southeast Asia. They

recognized that economic and social progress are essential for political stability. They welcomed the continuing contribution which mutual assistance under the Colombo plan affords throughout southeast Asia to these aims; and they agreed that there and elsewhere throughout the less developed areas of the world the best hope of peace, stability and political freedom lies in practical international co-operation of this kind.
7.	The ministers reviewed the world economic situation. They noted that, while in general the outlook was favourable, the economic expansion which had taken place since their last meeting had been greater in the industrialized countries of the commonwealth than in the primary producing countries. They agreed that an important condition of the prosperity of these countries was their ability to develop their export trade. They also recognized the urgent need to maintain and, where possible, increase the flow of economic assistance to the less developed countries. They welcomed the decision to establish an international development association.
8.	The ministers discussed European trade problems. They expressed concern at the prospect of any economic division in Europe and its possible political implications. The countries of Europe form an important market for commonwealth exports. The ministers expressed their hope that these countries would follow trade policies in accordance with the principles of the general agreement on tariffs and trade, and thus avoid damage to the economies of the primary producing countries and those that are also developing exports of manufactured goods. In addition, European countries have an important contribution to make in assisting the economic development of the less advanced countries. The ministers hoped that these problems could be speedily and satisfactorily resolved, with due regard to the interests of countries outside Europe.
9.	The commonwealth ministers reviewed the economic development of commonwealth countries in Africa which have recently attained or are approaching independence. They agreed that consideration should be given to the possibility of co-operative action among members of the commonwealth in assisting the economic development of these countries. This possibility will be studied in the first instance by officials of commonwealth governments, and the commonwealth economic consultative council will examine it at its next meeting.
10.	The ministers also reaffirmed their belief in the value of exchanges between commonwealth countries of persons with specialized skills and experience. They agreed that

further efforts should be made to foster and encourage these exchanges, whether on a regional or other basis, and that the commonwealth economic consultative council should take this question into urgent consideration. They trusted that employers in commonwealth countries-whether governments, statutory bodies or private companies-would be ready, wherever possible, to encourage members of their staffs to undertake a period of public service abroad and would do their best to ensure that their prospects in their home countries would not thereby be prejudiced.
11.	The ministers considered various questions of constitutional development within the commonwealth. They noted that the Federation of Nigeria would attain independence on 1st October, 1960. They extended to the federation their good wishes for its future and looked forward to welcoming an independent Nigeria as a member of the commonwealth on the completion of the necessary constitutional processes.
12.	The meeting was informed that, in pursuance of the recent plebiscite, the constituent assembly in Ghana had resolved that the necessary constitutional steps should be taken to introduce a republican form of constitution in Ghana by 1st July, 1960. In notifying this forthcoming constitutional change, the Prime Minister of Ghana assured the meeting of his country's desire to continue her membership of the commonwealth and her acceptance of the Queen as the symbol of the free association of its independent member nations and as such the head of the commonwealth. The heads of delegations of the other member countries of the commonwealth assured the Prime Minister of Ghana that the present relations between their countries and Ghana would remain unaffected by this constitutional change and they declared that their governments would accept and recognize Ghana's continued membership of the commonwealth.
13.	The meeting noted a statement by the South African Minister of External Affairs that the union government intended to hold a referendum on the subject of South Africa becoming a republic. The meeting affirmed the view that the choice between a monarchy and a republic was entirely the responsibility of the country concerned. In the event of South Africa deciding to become a republic and if the desire was subsequently expressed to remain a member of the commonwealth, the meeting suggested that the South African government should then ask for the consent

14.	The ministers reviewed the constitutional development of the commonwealth, with particular reference to the future of the smaller dependent territories. They agreed that a detailed study of this subject should be made for consideration by commonwealth governments.
15.	Whilst reaffirming the traditional practice that commonwealth conferences do not discuss the internal affairs of member
countries ministers availed themselves of Mr. Louw's presence in London to have informal discussions with him about the racial situation in South Africa. During these informal discussions Mr. Louw gave information and answered questions on the union's policies, and the other ministers conveyed to him their views on the South African problem. The ministers emphasized that the commonwealth itself is a multiracial association and expressed the need to ensure good relations between all member states and peoples of the commonwealth.
13th May, 1960.
